To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Associative-Cognitive Constructionist framework provides the best current understanding of SLA.

the Associative-Cognitive Constructionist model of SLA (CREED) provides the most comprehensive and empirically grounded framework for understanding SLA, that it is the only framework with a strong evidence base for its claims, and that it provides the most coherent and empirically well-supported framework for SLA pedagogy.
SLA involves the acquisition of language-specific constructions and that the endstate of SLA is limited by L1 entrenchments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ways in which the mind learns language, the ways that this learning is shaped by the social context of the learner, and the ways that this knowledge is put to use by the learner.
the ways in which the human brain learns language.
the question of how language learning works.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cognitive perspectives on SLA are currently in a state of rapid development and are highly promising.
the Associative-CognitiveCREED is the most comprehensive framework available for SLA research.
SLA is a natural cognitive process, and the Associative-Cognitive framework provides a coherent and detailed account of how that process works.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SLA is the process of learning to use language to communicate.

the Associative-Cognitive framework provides the best explanation of the data we have to date, that the framework has been successfully tested in many different domains, and that it has been used successfully in many different applications.
the CREED provides a coherent and empirically grounded theoretical basis for understanding SLA and its pedagogical implications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SLA is not special and is best viewed as the same type of learning process that underlies other areas of knowledge, such as the development of expertise.
SLA is an open-ended, lifelong process that is constrained by L1 entrenchments and that is optimally supported by socially mediated, scaffolded, explicit, and form-focused feedback.
language learning is not a mysterious process but rather one that is fully explicable in terms of the same associative and cognitive principles that govern all human learning.
